title: Cosine Similarity
statement: Implement `cosine(a, b)` for two equal-length, non-zero vectors. Return the dot product divided by the product of Euclidean norms. The result lies between -1 and 1 and ignores magnitude, which is why embedding search uses it.
constraints: Vectors are non-zero and equal length

approaches.name: Normalized dot
approaches.explanation: cos θ = (a · b) / (‖a‖ ‖b‖). Pre-normalized embeddings reduce this to a dot product.

editorial: Cosine similarity is the dot product of two L2-normalized vectors. It answers 'do these point the same way?' and ignores length, so a long document and a short query can still match in bag-of-words space. If either vector is the zero vector the denominator vanishes; production retrieval stacks should drop or specially handle those rows. Numerically, compute norms from the sum of squares and take one square root each.
